entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Euphronios of Autun was a bishop of Autun between 450 and 490, playing a pivotal role in the Christianization of Gaul. Under his leadership, the bishopric of Autun emerged as a major center of Christian learning and culture, attracting scholars and theologians from across Europe.

As a key figure in the early Christian Church, Euphronios of Autun was instrumental in shaping the theological debates of his time, including the Christological disputes that would shape Western Christendom. His writings and teachings had a lasting impact on the development of Christian doctrine and practice, influencing generations of theologians and church leaders to come.

Despite the passing of centuries, Euphronios of Autun's legacy continues to be felt in the modern era, with his writings and teachings remaining a valuable resource for scholars and theologians seeking to understand the early Christian Church and its ongoing impact on Western society.

In 1962, the Vatican's Pontifical Council for the Study of the Patristic Texts published a critical edition of Euphronios' writings, shedding new light on the life and thought of this enigmatic bishop.
